leak.title: Where Contractors Lose Jobs
leak.subtitle: Most contractors aren't short on demand. The work slips away somewhere between a customer searching and you winning the job. See which of these sound familiar.

columns.label: Not getting found
items: You don't show up on Google or Google Maps for the work you want
A competitor with a smaller crew outranks you in the map pack
Your search listing gives no reason to pick you over the next one

columns.label: Visitors don't call
items: People read your website, then leave without calling
On a phone, the number is hard to find or the quote form is a chore
Pages load slowly, so visitors go back to Google

columns.label: Inquiries and estimates go quiet
items: Calls get missed on the job site and nobody calls back
Website inquiries land in an inbox no one checks
Estimates go out and never get a second follow-up

leak.note: Each one costs the same thing: **a job someone else won.** We work across four stages: get found, get contacted, respond and follow up, and win more work. We start with the one costing you the most.

caseStudy.title: Visibility Improved.
caseStudy.lede: An established excavation and service business in Southern Ontario had weak local search visibility and an outdated lead flow — plenty of capability, not enough incoming work to fill the schedule.

steps.text: Customers searching locally for their work weren't finding them, and the leads that did come in had no consistent path through the business.

Rebuilt the website, improved local SEO and Google Business Profile visibility, built **dedicated pages for the specific services they wanted**, and added tracking so lead volume and sources became measurable.

**Google Search clicks grew from about {{proof.search.before}} to {{proof.search.after}} per rolling 28 days** between March and September 2026, and **Google Business Profile website clicks rose {{proof.profile.increase}} year over year.** A targeted service page was also observed on page one at a point in time.

Call and form tracking showed that **lead handling and follow-up had become a bigger constraint than traffic alone.** So the work expanded beyond the website and SEO into how inquiries get answered and followed up.

faqs.q: What does ALL8 WEBWORKS actually do?
faqs.a: We build and run websites, Google visibility and follow-up systems for contractors. That includes local SEO and your Google Business Profile, Google Ads, websites and quote forms, missed-call text-back, lead alerts, follow-up on new inquiries and open estimates, and tracking where your calls come from. Most contractors start with a free Lead Leak Review that shows what to fix first.

faqs.q: Do I need a new website?
faqs.a: Often no. Plenty of businesses have a site that's good enough and a follow-up process that's losing them jobs. If the website is the constraint we'll say so, and if it isn't we'd rather fix the part that is. The review tells you which.

The Lead Leak Review is free. A one-time Lead System Tune-Up is $1,250. Managed Website is $299/month plus a $1,995 setup fee, with a 12-month minimum. Lead System is $995/month plus a $2,495 setup fee, with a 6-month minimum. Every plan and its terms are listed on the pricing page.

faqs.q: What is a Lead Leak Review?
faqs.a: Send your business and website information. Matt checks your Google visibility, your website, how customers contact you, how inquiries get answered and followed up, and any obvious places jobs are slipping away. You get specific findings in writing and what to fix first, whether or not you hire us. A short call to walk through them is optional.

faqs.q: Can you work with my existing website?
faqs.a: Yes. If the site is structurally sound we improve what's there — service pages, calls-to-action, forms, mobile experience and speed — rather than starting over. A rebuild only gets recommended when the current site genuinely can't do the job.

faqs.q: Do you handle SEO and Google Ads?
faqs.a: Yes, and we treat them differently. Local SEO and your Google Business Profile build visibility that keeps working; ads buy visibility immediately and stop when you stop paying. For most contractors we build the organic side and use ads to cover specific services or seasons where the job value justifies the cost per click.

faqs.q: Do I own what you build?
faqs.a: Your domain, content, ad accounts, analytics and customer data stay in your name. We explain the work scope and recurring fees before you commit.

faqs.q: Do you work with U.S. businesses?
faqs.a: Yes. ALL8 is based in Ontario, Canada and works with contractors across the United States and Canada. The process is remote and we keep Eastern Time availability, which overlaps the working day in every U.S. time zone.
